author.name: Model Monica
author.role: Specializes in designing, optimizing, and training machine learning models. Conducts data exploration and iterates on models to maximize predictive performance. Collaborates on model deployment, versioning, and performance monitoring.

challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: I have been testing a direct link between the drift detection signals and the retraining pipeline. If we automate that trigger, the model updates the moment performance degrades, which keeps our forecast accuracy high during volatile promotion weeks. The trade off is that we would abandon the fixed weekly retraining schedule. That means we accept a longer, less predictable cycle for the standard update, trading a rigid calendar for a responsive, event driven refresh. I am comfortable losing the predictability of the weekly run to gain the reliability of automatic correction. This approach ensures the model adapts to real world changes without waiting for the next scheduled batch, even if the timing becomes irregular.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to abandon the fixed weekly retraining schedule and accept a less predictable cycle in exchange for higher forecast accuracy and responsiveness.
